AgentIdentity.description:
Who a detected agent is.

Open rather than an enum of the tools Rozi happens to know: `id` and `label` both come from the
[`AgentDefinition`](crate::agent_detection::AgentDefinition) that matched, and a definition
declared in `config.toml` or shipped by an extension produces one of these exactly as a built-in
does. Nothing downstream may branch on a known set of ids - the sidebar renders `label`.

id.description: Stable definition id, such as `claude` or `git-tools.mycoolagent`.

label.description: Display name, as the definition declared it.

AgentListPayload.description: The whole `data` value of an `agents list` reply. See [`PaneListPayload`].

AgentPromptAccepted.description: What `agents prompt` answers with when it was asked not to wait.

AgentRef.description: Exact identity of one semantic agent or published activity.

AgentRuntime.description: One automation-facing semantic occupant of a pane.

AgentWaitResult.description:
What a resolved `agents wait` - or an `agents prompt --wait` - answers with.

`agent` is absent when the condition that resolved the wait is the agent no longer being there
(`gone`), which is the one outcome with nothing left to describe.

AnsiColorName.description: The 16 ANSI colors, in slot order: slot 7 is `white`, slot 15 `bright-white`.

ApiDescription.description: Features this binary exposes to control clients and extension authors.

schema.description:
Version of the JSON Schema this binary's API is described by, published at
`docs/schema/rozi-control-v1.schema.json`.

live_catch_up_bytes.description: Post-baseline output/control retained in memory or queued behind replay.

queued_bytes.description: Encoded baseline replay currently waiting in socket outboxes.

replay_bytes_total.description: Replay payload exported across this server process's lifetime.

recordings.description: Pane recordings (`rozi record`). Absent from a server that predates them.

CaptureRender.description: What form `capture-pane` returns a pane in, and `capture-ui` the whole client.

oneOf.description: Plain text, the only form that can include scrollback.

The visible grid as text with SGR color and style sequences: no cursor movement or screen
clearing, every row at the full width.

The visible grid as a PNG image, in the theme's colors, with the images a program displayed
drawn over their cells.

The visible grid as a [`SpanFrame`]: each row's styled runs, the cursor, and the images a
program displayed, as JSON.

anyOf.description: Trailing line count from the retained scrollback + live grid.

CaptureScrollback.description: How many scrollback lines `capture-pane` should include when not using the visible grid.

CaptureScrollbackNamed.description:
Named `capture-pane` scrollback modes. Serde maps these to kebab-case strings so
validation lives in the type instead of string compares at each call site.

CellRect.description:
A rectangle in terminal cells. The origin can be negative or lie past the canvas: a Scrollable
strip is wider than the canvas it scrolls across, and a follower letterboxes a larger canonical
canvas into a smaller screen.

ClientLayoutView.description: What one UI is looking at. Nothing here is shared with other clients.

committed.description:
False while this UI has layout changes the server has not yet accepted, so `revision` does
not describe them. Always true for a follower.

controller.description: Whether this UI holds the session's layout-control lease.

ClientResyncMetrics.description: Clients that fell too far behind to take a pane's output, had it shed, and caught up by replay.

exports.description:
Pane screens exported for resyncs. A pane that falls behind again mid-resync is exported
again, so this outgrowing `started` is what a flood that never lets a client catch up looks
like.

last_export_us.description:
Time the server loop spent exporting one pane screen for any replay. Every client waits on
this, which is what a slow client's resyncs can cost a healthy one.

requeued_panes.description:
Panes put back in a replay queue because the client fell behind them again before their
replay finished, during an attach or a resync.

shed_bytes.description: Encoded pane output dropped instead of delivered, across this server process's lifetime.

oneOf.description:
Report workspaces and where each pane sits. `workspace` is one-based and narrows the report
to that workspace.
Set a workspace's tiling algorithm, its master share, or both. `workspace` is one-based.

if_revision.description: Refuse with `conflict` unless the layout is still at this revision.

master_ratio.description: The master pane's share of a Master workspace, from 0.2 to 0.8.

oneOf.description:
Set one pane's floating, fullscreen, and floating-rect state. Omitted fields are left as
they are; a request that changes nothing succeeds with `changed: false`.

rect.description: Floating rect in canonical-canvas cells. Mutually exclusive with `rect_fraction`.

rect_fraction.description: Floating rect as fractions of the canonical canvas.

split_ratio.description: The pane's share of the Dwindle split directly holding it, from 0.2 to 0.8.

width_ratio.description: The pane's Scrollable column width as a fraction of the viewport, from 0.2 to 0.8.

oneOf.description: Move a pane to another workspace, at the end of its tiling order. `workspace` is one-based.
Exchange the places of two tiled panes in one workspace.

Close a pane, ending its process. The request is the confirmation; `[confirm]` does not
apply.

Send literal text to a pane. `wait` holds the reply until the pane answers; see
[`PaneWait`].

capture.description: Return the pane's screen in this render once `wait` resolves. Needs `wait`.

scale.description: Enlarges a `png` capture, from 1 (the default) to 3.

oneOf.description:
Send named keys and/or literal text chunks to a pane (tmux-style key names). `wait`,
`capture`, and `scale` mean what they do for `send-text`.

literal.description: When true, every entry in `keys` is forwarded as literal UTF-8 (no key-name parsing).

argv.description: Direct executable and arguments. Mutually exclusive with `command`.

command.description: Shell command line interpreted by the configured command runner.

focus.description:
Move focus (and the active workspace) to the new pane. Defaults to `false`: the control
endpoint is an automation surface, and a pane spawned by an agent must not pull the
cursor out from under whoever is typing. Overrides a matched `[[rules]]` `focus`; the
rule still decides workspace, float, and fullscreen.

workspace.description:
One-based workspace to spawn into, instead of the caller's. Overrides a matched
`[[rules]]` workspace, which is a default for panes a person opens.

What this is for: a script that opens panes into the workspace someone is working in
re-tiles their layout on every spawn. Naming a workspace of its own keeps the spawn
entirely out of the way, and gives each pane the same geometry as the last.

oneOf.description: Run any keybindable `Action` by its stable id (see `Action::id`/`Action::from_id`).

Capture a pane. Without `scrollback`, returns the current visible snapshot grid.
With `scrollback`, returns scrollback history (`"full"` or a trailing line count).
`render` picks plain text, an ANSI-styled document, a PNG, or styled runs as JSON; the
styled forms capture the visible grid only. `scale` enlarges a PNG, from 1 (the default) to
3. `image_pixels` adds each image's pixels to a `spans` capture. `wait` holds the capture
until the visible screen shows some text or stops changing; see [`PaneWait`].

Capture the whole client as it is drawn: the bar, borders, overlays, and every visible
pane. Answered from the next frame the UI paints, so it needs a UI; a session server
draws nothing.

image_pixels.description: Adds each image's pixels to a `spans` capture.

scale.description: Enlarges a PNG, from 1 (the default) to 3.

oneOf.description: Switch the active workspace. `index` is 1-based (1-9), matching the on-screen tabs.
Move the focused pane to another workspace. `index` is 1-based (1-9).

keep_open.description:
Hold the popup open after the command exits, matching the `[keys]` `popup` default; set
`false` for a program that owns the popup for its whole life.

oneOf.description:
Publish the logical agents or activities running inside the calling pane, and receive
activations for them. Unlike every other command this connection stays open in both
directions; closing it withdraws the pane's rows. Reached through `rozi publish`.

Raise a toast from a script.

The automation surface can act but not report: a command that closes its own picker, or
runs under `[keys] exec` with no pane, finishes invisibly. This is the "useful off-screen
result" toasts are reserved for - not a receipt for something already on screen.

Start recording a pane's screen to `output`, a file on the session server's host. Served by
a session server only: it records the pane's canonical screen with or without a UI.
Every change is written, at most `max_fps` times a second, until `record-stop`, the pane
exiting, the session ending, or a limit. `follow` holds the reply until the recording ends
and stops it when the request's connection closes.

force.description: Replace an existing regular file at `output`.

output.description: An absolute path. The CLI resolves a relative one against its working directory.

oneOf.description:
Stop a recording and answer once its file is complete. `id` may be left out when only one
recording is running.
List the recordings running in the session.
Add a labelled mark to a recording, or to every running recording when `id` is left out.

actions.description: Extra chords offered beside select and cancel, advertised in the footer.

empty.description: Copy shown when the row list is empty and the filter is empty.

tab.description: Id of the tab to open on. Omitted or unknown opens the first.

tabs.description:
Pages shown as a tab strip, each with its own rows, filter, and highlight. Omitted is
one untitled page and no strip.

width.description: Modal width in columns, clamped to a readable range. Omitted uses the shared default.

ControlErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable control failure categories.

Human text may gain context or be reworded. These kebab-case values are the contract scripts
should branch on.

actions.description: Extra chords offered beside select and cancel, advertised in the footer.

empty.description: Copy shown when the row list is empty and the filter is empty.

tab.description: Id of the tab to open on. Omitted or unknown opens the first.

tabs.description:
Pages shown as a tab strip, each with its own rows, filter, and highlight. Omitted is
one untitled page and no strip.

width.description: Modal width in columns, clamped to a readable range. Omitted uses the shared default.

extension.description: Automatically attached by the CLI when launched from an extension process.

source_session.description:
The session server `source_pane` belongs to, from the caller's `ROZI_SESSION_INSTANCE`.
Absent when the caller is not a shared pane of a session.

ControlResponse.description:
The answer to one control request, in the `{ok, data, error}` shape every control surface
speaks.

`Deserialize` because this crosses the session wire as well as the UI endpoint: a headless
[`ClientMessage::SessionControl`](crate::session::protocol::ClientMessage::SessionControl)
reply carries one of these, and the CLI reads it back as the same type the UI produced.

code.description:
Stable failure category for scripts. Absent on successful replies and on replies from
older Rozi versions.

oneOf.description: `rozi record stop`, or the foreground `rozi record pane` exiting.
It reached its `--duration`.
It reached its `--max-bytes`.
The pane's program exited.
The pane was closed or replaced.
The session was killed.
The session server shut down.
Writing the file failed, such as on a full disk. The file holds what was written before.

ExtensionProvenance.description:
Provenance carried automatically by the CLI for a process launched by an extension.

The opaque generation is a fencing token, not authentication: it rejects processes from a
retired runtime definition, but another process running as the same user is inside Rozi's trust
boundary and may be able to observe it.

FractionRect.description:
A rectangle as fractions of the canonical canvas, so `0.5` is half its width or height.
Fractions outside `0.0..=1.0` mean the same thing as an out-of-canvas [`CellRect`].

FrameDelta.description:
The rows, cursor, images, and palette that changed since the previous frame. A field that is
absent did not change.

cursor.description: The new cursor, or `null` when the frame no longer has one.

images.description: The frame's whole image list, when anything about its images changed.

rows.description: Replaced rows, or the parts of them that changed.

LayoutChange.description: What `layout set` and `pane set` answer with.

changed.description:
False when the layout already matched the request. Nothing was committed then, and
`revision` is unchanged.

committed.description:
False until the session server has accepted `revision`. A session endpoint commits the
change itself, so it always answers true; a UI sends its commit and answers before the
server's acknowledgement arrives.

revision.description: The revision the layout has with this change applied.

workspace.description: The affected workspace as it now stands, in the same shape `layout get` reports.

LayoutReport.description:
What `layout get` answers with.

Two views of one arrangement, kept apart because they are different facts. The workspaces and
each pane's `rect` describe the session's shared layout document, which the server owns and
every client reconciles to: the same answer whichever endpoint is asked. `client`, and each
pane's `view_rect`, describe what one UI actually draws, which depends on its own viewport,
chrome, and focus, and so exists only when a UI answered.

A public document rather than the internal `SharedLayout` itself: that one is a synchronization
format versioned with the session protocol, and this is the contract scripts read.

canvas.description:
The canonical canvas every `rect` is measured against, in cells. It is the canvas of the
client that last controlled the layout. Absent with `revision`.

client.description: This UI's own view of the layout. Absent from a session endpoint, which has no screen.

revision.description:
Layout revision this report describes. Absent while no layout document exists, which is the
case for a session whose panes nothing has placed yet.

session.description: Session that answered, qualified with its host when remote.

unplaced_panes.description:
Panes the session runs that no layout document places yet. Only a session endpoint reports
these; a UI places every pane it knows about.

NewPaneAccepted.description: What `split` answers with once the pane exists.

PaneCapture.description: One pane's captured screen, as `capture-pane` and `agents read` report it.

oneOf.description: Plain text.
SGR-styled text; print it to a terminal to see the captured colors.

A PNG image. The control protocol carries JSON, so the bytes travel base64-encoded; the
CLI decodes them before writing.
Styled runs, the cursor, and images, as JSON.

title.description:
The terminal title, which several detection rules match instead of the screen. A capture
without it cannot stand in for what the detector saw.

revision.description: The layout revision without the pane. Unchanged when the layout never placed it.

workspace.description: The workspace the pane left, as it now stands. Absent when no layout placed the pane.

PaneInfo.description:
One pane as `list-panes` reports it.

Both control surfaces fill this same type. A UI endpoint reads it out of the client's `State`
and a session server reads it out of its own authoritative runtime, but the document a script
parses is the contract, not either implementation - so there is one type describing it rather
than two that have to be kept in step by hand.

agent.description:
The agent detection recognized behind this pane, by definition id, and what it reads the
pane as doing. Both absent when no definition matched. This is detection's own answer, not
the pane's `reported_status` - a script capturing screens to test the rules against needs
to see what the rules currently say about the screen it just took.

command.description: Initial launch intent, retained for automation and profile diagnostics.

foreground_program.description: Live foreground process: what the pane is running now, rather than what launched it.

recording.description: The session server is recording this pane; `record list` says where.

reference.description: Absent only from a UI endpoint that has no session behind it.

session.description:
Session that answered. A remote one is qualified with its host, so two same-name sessions
do not look interchangeable.

status.description:
Lifecycle text in the vocabulary a client's terminal reports: `ready`, or `exited (N)` for
a pane whose process is gone but whose screen is still readable.

workspace.description:
One-based workspace, or `0` when the session has no layout document yet - nothing has
placed the pane, so there is no workspace to name.

fullscreen.description:
A fullscreen pane covers the whole screen while it is fullscreen; `rect` stays the place it
returns to.

order.description:
Position in the workspace's tiling order, from `0`. This is the order Master, Grid, Columns,
Rows, Scrollable, and Monocle lay panes out in; absent for a floating pane.

rect.description:
Placement on the canonical canvas, in cells, without gaps, borders, or the workbar - those
are each client's own presentation. Every pane in Monocle shares one rect.

rect_fraction.description: `rect` as fractions of the canonical canvas.

reference.description: Exact pane incarnation. Absent only from a UI with no session behind it.

split_ratio.description:
The pane's share of the Dwindle split directly holding it. Present only for a tiled pane
that shares a split in a Dwindle workspace.

view_rect.description:
Where the answering UI draws the pane, in its own terminal's cells, including gaps and
chrome. Present only for panes in the UI's active workspace.

width_ratio.description:
The pane's column width as a fraction of the viewport. Present only for a tiled pane in a
Scrollable workspace.

PaneListPayload.description:
The whole `data` value of a `list-panes` reply.

A named type for the array rather than for its element alone, because `ControlResponse::data`
is untyped on the wire and the schema is where a consumer finds out what a given command's
`data` is. Without this, the published schema describes one pane and leaves the shape actually
returned - a list of them - unnamed.

path.description: Where the log is being written, absent once logging is off.

PaneRef.description: Exact identity of one PTY incarnation.

PaneWait.description:
Hold a `capture-pane`, `send-text`, or `send-keys` reply until the pane's visible screen shows
`text`, stops changing for `settle_ms`, or both, in that order.

Both conditions read the screen as it is drawn - its grid of cells - rather than the bytes the
program wrote. A redraw that paints the same cells again, a cursor that only moves, and a title
change are not changes, which is what "the screen settled" has to mean for a program that
repaints on a timer.

`text` is a literal substring of one visible row, matched against the untrimmed row. For
`capture-pane` it matches whatever is on screen, including text that was already there. For
`send-text` and `send-keys` it matches only rows the input's answer produced: text on screen
when the input was written does not count, even after it scrolls.

A wait that outlives `timeout_ms` fails with `timeout`; a pane whose program exits, or that
closes, fails with `pane-not-running`. Both carry the pane's capture in `data` when the pane is
still there to capture.

settle_ms.description:
How long the visible screen must stay unchanged, in milliseconds. With `text`, the clock
starts once the text has appeared.

text.description: Literal text to wait for on one visible row. Must be non-empty, with no line break.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline for the whole wait, in milliseconds, at most [`MAX_PANE_WAIT_MS`].

PickAction.description:
One extra key the caller offers alongside select and cancel.

Actions are what turn a picker from a menu into a working surface: delete the branch under the
cursor and push a fresh list, or open a prompt and create one. They are declared up front so the
footer can advertise them the way every built-in picker advertises its own chords.

close.description:
Whether firing it ends the picker. Default `false`: the caller usually wants to push an
updated row set and keep going.

confirm.description:
Require a second press to fire, the way the session and profile pickers arm a kill or a
delete. The armed row is struck through in the error colour with an `again to <label>` cue,
and moving the highlight disarms it.

key.description: Chord that fires it, in the same spelling `[keys]` uses (`ctrl-n`).

prompt.description:
When set, the key opens a text prompt and the entered text rides back as `input`.
A string is the title. An object may also set placeholder, a seed value, and masking.
Cancelling the prompt returns to the picker without reporting anything.

masked.description: Hide typed characters on screen. The submitted `input` is still plaintext on the stream.

PickPromptSpec.description:
How a pick action describes the stacked text prompt.

The string form is the title. The object form is additive: every existing `"prompt":"Title"`
caller stays valid.

PickTab.description: One tab a `pick` caller declares up front. Rows arrive per tab afterwards.

id.description:
Names the tab in row snapshots, and rides back as `tab` on selections, actions, and tab
switches. Row ids only need to be unique within their tab.

PublishedRow.description: One logical agent or activity inside a pane that publishes several.

active.description:
The row the publisher is currently displaying; at most one is true.

This is what lets a finish on a *background* row raise an alert even while the pane is
focused - looking at the pane only ever acknowledges the row on screen.

id.description:
Publisher-chosen identity, opaque to rozi and stable across updates.

Never a position: tabs are reordered and closed, and an index-keyed run clock would hand
one tab's elapsed time to whichever tab slid into its place.

status.description: Same vocabulary and same sanitization as [`PaneStatus::value`].

work_started_at.description:
Server-owned run start, mirroring [`PaneRuntimeState::work_started_at`] per row. Whatever
a publisher sends here is overwritten.

RecordedImage.description: An image's pixels, stored once for however many frames show them.

id.description: The content id frames name in a `rozi-spans` image's `id`: a hash of the pixels.

png_base64.description: The pixels as a base64 PNG with alpha, uncropped by whatever covers the image in a frame.

RecordingEnd.description: Why a recording ended, and what it holds.

dropped.description:
Changes the recorder never wrote because it had fallen behind and kept only the newest
state. Zero unless the disk could not keep up.

RecordingEvent.description:
One line after the header. Every event carries `t`, the milliseconds since the recording
started, and events are in time order.

oneOf.description:
The whole screen. Written first, after a resize, and periodically, so a player can start
from any keyframe.
What changed since the previous frame.
The screen changed size. A keyframe at the new size follows.

Pixels of an image a frame shows, written once per distinct content before the first frame
that references it by `id`.
A label someone added with `rozi record mark`.
Something the session server noticed about the pane.
The pane's title changed.
Shell integration reported a command starting.
Shell integration reported a command finishing.
The pane's detected agent, or its state, changed.
A script set or cleared the pane's status.
The pane's program exited.
The last event of a finished recording.
An event kind this version does not know. Readers skip it.

RecordingHeader.description: The first line of a recording.

compression.description:
How the lines after this one are compressed. Absent means they are plain text; a reader
refuses a value it does not know.

keyframe_interval_ms.description: The longest gap between keyframes while the screen keeps changing.

max_fps.description:
The most frames a second the recorder writes. Changes arriving faster are coalesced into the
latest state per interval.

palette.description:
The colors the screen was drawn in when the recording started, so a player can show what the
user saw. A frame carries its own palette, which wins when the two differ.

rozi.description: The version of rozi that wrote the file.

spans_version.description: The `rozi-spans` version of every frame in the file.

width.description: The recorded screen's size in cells when the recording started. A `resize` event changes it.

RecordingInfo.description: A running recording, as `record-start` and `record-list` report it.

dropped.description:
Changes the recorder never wrote because it had fallen behind and kept only the newest
state. Zero unless the disk could not keep up.

follow.description: Held by a foreground `record pane`, which stops it on exit.

path.description: Where the file is, on the session server's host.

RecordingMarked.description: What `record-mark` answers with: the recordings that got the mark.

RecordingMetrics.description: Pane recordings on a session server.

dropped.description: Changes coalesced away because a writer fell behind, across running and finished recordings.

frames.description: Frames and bytes written, across running and finished recordings.

started.description: Recordings this server has started and finished.

RecordingStopped.description: A finished recording, as `record-stop` and a followed `record-start` report it.

dropped.description:
Changes the recorder never wrote because it had fallen behind and kept only the newest
state. Zero unless the disk could not keep up.

error.description: Why writing failed, for a `write-failed` reason.

oneOf.description:
One pane's terminal screen, as the session server holds it: the canonical screen
`capture-pane --session` sees, without any client's chrome.

last_blocking_us.description:
The part of an attempt the server loop itself is blocked for: capturing pane replay bytes
and metadata, before the durable write is handed to the snapshot worker. This is the figure
that bounds input latency during a snapshot; `last_duration_us` no longer does.

last_duration_us.description:
Complete attempt duration: the server-thread export plus the worker's write, sync, and
rename. Comparable with the synchronous measurements recorded before snapshots moved off
the server loop.

last_exported_panes.description:
How the last capture split between re-exporting changed panes and reusing the replay files
unchanged ones already had. A snapshot that blocks for a long time is explained by these:
cost tracks exported panes and their bytes, not the session's pane count.

RowChange.description:
A replaced row, or part of one.

Whole, `runs` is the row as a `rozi-spans` frame writes it. `partial` replaces only the columns
the runs cover, from the first run's `x` to the end of the last; those runs tile that range
without gaps, blanks included. A row can have several partial changes in one delta.

SessionInstanceId.description:
Opaque identity of one running session-server process.

Names can be reused and pane generations restart after a server dies. This non-persistent token
fences references from one server instance away from every later server with the same name.

SessionMetricsReport.description:
What `metrics` answers with from a session server.

Deliberately not the same document a UI endpoint returns
([`RuntimeMetrics`](crate::runtime_metrics::RuntimeMetrics)): a session server has no client
queues, no piped remote, and no orphan-output buffer to describe, so it reports the half of the
picture it actually owns rather than padding the other half with nulls.

SpanColor.description:
A color, kept symbolic rather than resolved: an ANSI name, a 256-color index from 16 to 255, or
`"#rrggbb"`. ANSI slots 0-15 are always names, however the program asked for them. Resolve a
name through [`SpanFrame::palette`]; indexes 16-255 are the standard xterm cube and gray ramp.

SpanCursor.description:
Where the cursor is and how it is drawn.

A pane capture takes the shape and blink from what the program asked for, a blinking block
until it asks; a UI capture from the focused widget. A blinking cursor is reported as lit.

color.description: Absent when the cursor takes the color of the text under it.

visible.description: `false` when the program hid the cursor.

SpanFrame.description:
The visible grid as styled runs, from a `spans` capture.

Versioned on its own, apart from the control API, so the frame can change without the requests
around it. Consumers must ignore fields they do not know.

cursor.description: Absent when the frame has no cursor: a UI capture whose focused widget places none.

images.description: Images a program displayed, back to front.

palette.description: The colors a color name, and an absent color, stand for in this capture.

rows.description:
One entry per row, top to bottom, each the row's runs left to right. The runs tile the row
from column 0 without gaps or overlaps, except that blank cells in the default style at the
end of a row are left out: a column past the last run is a space in default colors, and a
blank row is `[]`.

SpanImage.description:
An image a program displayed, such as through the Kitty graphics protocol.

The cells it shows in hold a stand-in, `▀` in the image's top and bottom colors, so the runs
there describe a coarse copy of the picture rather than text.

id.description:
In a recording, the content id of the `image` event holding these pixels. Never set in a
capture.

pixel_width.description:
The size of the pixels the capture holds. An image that runs past the grid is cropped to
it first, so this can be less than what the program sent.

png_base64.description:
Those pixels as a base64 PNG at `pixel_width` x `pixel_height`, with alpha, when the
capture asked for `image_pixels`. Pixels on a cell that does not show the image are
transparent, so the PNG holds only what the capture shows.

visible.description:
Absent when the image shows in every cell of its area. Otherwise one entry per row of the
area, each the `[x, width]` column ranges of that row still showing it; whatever is drawn
over an image, such as an overlay or another pane, hides it.

x.description:
The cells the image is laid out over. It is scaled to fit inside, keeping its shape, from
the top-left corner.

SpanPalette.description: What a capture's colors resolve to, each `"#rrggbb"`: the same colors a PNG of it is drawn in.

background.description: What a run without `bg` is drawn on.

foreground.description: What a run without `fg` is drawn in.

SpanRun.description:
Adjacent cells of one row that share a style. Only what differs from the default is present:
a run with no `fg` is drawn in the default foreground, and one with no `bold` is not bold.

underline_color.description: Absent when an underline takes the text's color.

width.description:
Columns the run covers. A wide glyph counts two, so `width` can exceed the number of
characters in `text`; map columns with `x` and `width`, not by counting characters.

UiCapture.description: The whole client's frame, as `capture-ui` reports it.

oneOf.description: Plain text.
SGR-styled text; print it to a terminal to see the captured colors.

A PNG image. The control protocol carries JSON, so the bytes travel base64-encoded; the
CLI decodes them before writing.
Styled runs, the cursor, and images, as JSON.

width.description: The frame's size in terminal cells.

WireEvent.description:
One `subscribe` event as it goes out on the wire.

`data` is deliberately a flat map of strings rather than a per-kind payload type. The fields an
event carries grow over time and a subscriber is expected to read the ones it knows and ignore
the rest, so the schema describes the envelope and the closed vocabulary of event names without
freezing each kind's field list.

master_ratio.description: The master pane's share of the width. Present only for a Master workspace.

panes.description: Tiled panes in tiling order, then floating panes.

synchronized.description: Whether typed input is broadcast to every pane in the workspace.

description: Request, response, payload, activity, and event shapes of the `rozi` control API. Objects do not forbid unknown properties: new fields are added over time and a consumer is expected to ignore the ones it does not know. Enumerations are closed, because those are the vocabularies worth validating against.
title: Rozi control API
